column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
sanxingdui-museum|9.5,9.7,9.8,9.5,9.2|-|Remarkable Bronze Age assemblages justify elite uniqueness, but one museum's visitor reach need not exceed the Forbidden City.

dujiangyan-irrigation-system|9.1,9.6,9.8,9.0,8.6|-|Exceptional ancient engineering system with worldwide impact; an infrastructure visit is less immediately immersive than large heritage palace ensembles.
leshan-giant-buddha|9.2,9.7,9.7,9.2,8.1|-|Immense singular carved Buddha with rich history, but one monument has narrower depth than a comprehensive pilgrimage complex.
victoria-harbour|9.3,9.3,8.8,9.6,9.0|-|Extraordinary city/harbour panorama, yet skyline scenery is not equivalent to unique ancient archaeological significance.
xian-city-wall|9.1,9.4,9.6,9.2,8.8|-|Exceptional complete urban fortifications with traversable perimeter, below Great Wall stretches in global singularity.
historic-centre-macau|9.1,9.4,9.5,9.1,9.2|-|Important Sino-Portuguese urban fabric with multiple monuments; heritage significance should be below world-defining imperial sites.
mount-everest-north-base-camp|9.6,9.5,9.1,8.7,8.0|-|World's highest mountain gives immense visual impact, but base-camp stop is not equivalent to climbing Everest or exploring the massif.
mount-kailash|9.6,9.8,9.7,8.8,8.5|-|Globally significant sacred mountain and pilgrimage landscape, with experience and depth separate from the summit and whole region.
gulangyu-island|9.2,9.2,9.0,9.2,9.0|-|Distinctive historic island with layered architecture but not as globally consequential as top UNESCO urban ensembles.
fujian-tulou-yongding|9.5,9.6,9.5,9.3,9.0|-|Rare communal earthen buildings and living heritage; group visitor breadth below citywide historic ensembles.
dazu-rock-carvings|9.5,9.7,9.8,9.3,8.9|-|Exceptionally important dispersed Buddhist carvings, though travel between components changes visitor depth from a single museum.
wudang-mountains|9.4,9.6,9.7,9.3,9.1|-|Exceptional Daoist sacred landscape with historic monasteries, but not every field needs near-perfect score.
stone-forest-shilin|9.2,9.4,8.9,9.3,8.6|-|Exceptional limestone formations with scenic depth, but world-geology significance is below iconic reference sites such as Huangshan.
temple-of-heaven|9.5,9.6,9.8,9.5,9.1|-|Extraordinary imperial ritual park, yet slightly less singular than the Forbidden City complex.
great-wall-jiankou|9.5,9.6,9.4,9.0,8.3|-|Dramatic wild Great Wall stretch, but difficult, fragmented visitor experience and scale differ from Jinshanling.
pingyao-ancient-city|9.1,9.4,9.6,9.2,9.1|-|Exceptionally preserved historic trading city, with much stronger urban breadth than a single city gate.
zhangye-danxia|9.4,9.7,8.9,9.5,8.6|-|Extraordinary colored hills and geology but controlled scenic stops have narrower depth than huge protected landscapes.

badain-jaran-desert|9.4,9.7,9.0,9.3,9.1|-|Keep rare mega-dune and interdunal-lake landscape, newly UNESCO-inscribed and internationally exceptional in geomorphology; slightly moderate experience and depth relative to a fully visitable multi-site landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1638/

forbidden-city|9.9,9.9,10.0,9.8,9.5|-|Retain exact approved worldwide significance ten: Ming-Qing imperial palace preserves unparalleled ensemble architectural layout and cultural history, unlike smaller palace or ceremonial complexes. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/439

great-wall-jinshanling|10.0,10.0,10.0,9.8,9.2|-|Retain exact registered ten anchors for engineering impact, uniqueness and global heritage: exceptional preserved and hikeable Ming wall system at a prime Great Wall section. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/438

great-wall-mutianyu|9.8,9.8,9.9,9.7,9.0|-|Retain extraordinary, coherent, frequently visited Great Wall mountain-fortification section, though less singular in adventure and scale than the designated Jinshanling reference. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/438

huanglong-scenic-area|9.5,9.7,9.1,9.6,9.1|-|Retain globally unusual travertine pools, waterfalls and forest mountain setting, geographically and scientifically separate from Jiuzhaigou rather than a generic mountain viewpoint. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/638

jiuzhaigou-valley|9.8,9.7,9.4,9.8,9.1|-|Retain exceptional lakes, waterfalls and alpine forest recognized internationally as a globally defining protected landscape; existing category nature ten remains an approved anchor. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/637

jokhang-temple|9.3,9.8,9.9,9.2,8.6|-|Retain centuries of Tibetan Buddhist religious centrality with meaningful architecture and pilgrim tradition, a discrete component of the Potala UNESCO ensemble rather than a substitute for the whole city. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707

kanas-lake|8.8,9.0,8.4,8.9,8.4|nature=9.1|Scenic glacial alpine lake and forests but international comparisons with Jiuzhaigou and large lake systems do not support extraordinary uniqueness or world-class category nature 9.5 for the lake alone. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/637

kashgar-old-city|8.8,8.8,8.7,8.9,8.6|architecture=8.8,culture=9.1|Exceptionally significant Silk Road and living Uyghur urban identity, but substantial demolition and tourism-oriented rebuilding reduce authenticity of the built historic fabric; cannot equate the present old-city streets with an intact medieval UNESCO city. Source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0016718521003328

li-river-guilin|9.7,9.8,9.1,9.7,9.2|-|Retain globally exceptional navigable karst river-landscape and iconic limestone towers; compare against Ha Long Bay's partly submerged tower-karst rather than a local riverboat outing. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

longmen-grottoes|9.7,9.9,9.9,9.6,9.2|-|Retain vast cliff-carved sculptural gallery with thousands of niches and internationally influential Buddhist art, not comparable to one standalone cave shrine. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1003

mogao-caves|9.8,9.9,9.9,9.5,9.4|-|Retain exceptional 492-site cave sanctuary heritage and a millennium of Buddhist murals and sculpture, far broader and more consequential than an ordinary visitor cave. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/440

mount-huangshan|9.9,9.9,9.6,9.8,9.3|-|Retain approved world-defining nature and photography category anchors for extraordinary granite peaks, cloudscapes and landscape-cultural influence. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

potala-palace|9.8,9.9,9.9,9.4,9.2|-|Retain emblematic Tibetan religious and royal architectural complex at Lhasa with extraordinary historical and artistic significance; Jokhang remains individually scored, not copied into palace depth. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707

summer-palace|9.5,9.7,9.7,9.5,9.2|-|Beijing's exceptionally extensive imperial garden landscape is globally distinguished, but historical singularity and scope should remain slightly below the capital's Forbidden City palace nucleus. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/880/

terracotta-army|9.9,10.0,10.0,9.7,9.1|-|Retain exact approved uniqueness and significance tens for Qin imperial life-size army and world-defining funerary archaeological assemblage; the pit museum is narrower in visit depth than full mausoleum region. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/441

yungang-grottoes|9.6,9.9,9.9,9.6,9.0|-|Retain exceptional 5th-6th century carved Buddhist caves and mature sculptural styles, with global comparison to Mogao and Longmen rather than small local rock shrines. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/cn

zhangjiajie-national-forest-park|9.8,9.7,9.3,9.8,9.3|-|Retain iconic forest of sandstone pinnacles with extraordinary visual experience and park-level multi-trail discovery; geological landforms supported within UNESCO Wulingyuan. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/640
